title: Monster Stats
body:
Goal: store a game monster in a dictionary and look things up by name.

{"name": "Blobby", "level": 1, "health": 30, "attack": 4, "speed": 2}
   key      value
  1. Open starter.py and press Run.
  2. TODO 1: loop with for key, value in monster.items(): and build lines like health: 30.
  3. TODO 2: finish level_up().
  4. Run it and type magic when it asks for a stat. KeyError! That is this week's bug hunt. TODO 3: check if stat in monster: first.

Done looks like:

name: Blobby
level: 1
health: 30
attack: 4
speed: 2
color: bluish green
Blobby eats a glowing mushroom... LEVEL UP!
name: Blobby
level: 2
health: 40
attack: 6
...
Which stat do you want to look up? magic
magic: 0

Extra: make a second monster and write battle(a, b) that returns the name of the one with the higher attack.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Read the three TODO comments in starter.py. A dictionary stores each value under a name, called a key. Run the program and see which part is still empty.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: monster.items() gives you each key with its value, so a loop can use both. An f-string like f"{____}: {____}" builds a line of text. To avoid a KeyError, check that the stat is in the monster before you look it up.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: In stat_report(), use lines.append(____) inside the loop. In level_up(), copy the pattern of the level line: monster["health"] = monster["health"] + ____. In get_stat(), only look the stat up when your check passes. Otherwise give back the value the docstring names.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Monster Stats
# A monster is stored in a dictionary: keys (names) and values.


def make_monster(name):
    """Return a new level-1 monster as a dictionary."""
    return {"name": name, "level": 1, "health": 30, "attack": 4, "speed": 2}


def stat_report(monster):
    """Return a list of lines like "health: 30", one for every key."""
    lines = []
    # TODO 1: for key, value in monster.items():
    #             append an f-string like "health: 30" to lines
    return lines


def level_up(monster):
    """Make the monster stronger: +1 level, +10 health, +2 attack. Return it."""
    monster["level"] = monster["level"] + 1
    # TODO 2: add 10 to health and 2 to attack, the same way.
    return monster


def get_stat(monster, stat):
    """Return the value of a stat, or 0 if the monster does not have it."""
    # TODO 3 (bug hunt): looking up a key that is not there crashes with KeyError.
    # Check first:  if stat in monster:
    return monster[stat]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    blobby = make_monster("Blobby")
    blobby["color"] = "bluish green"      # adding a new key is easy
    for line in stat_report(blobby):
        print(line)
    print("Blobby eats a glowing mushroom... LEVEL UP!")
    level_up(blobby)
    for line in stat_report(blobby):
        print(line)
    stat = input("Which stat do you want to look up? ")
    print(f"{stat}: {get_stat(blobby, stat)}")
